title: Seven SIU investigators probe death of air traveller:
article: Investigators hope autopsy results expected today will reveal why a 43-year-old man who flew to Ottawa airport from Halifax on the weekend died while being detained by police and treated by paramedics.

Stephane Michaud, a passenger on a Sunday morning Air Canada flight from Halifax to Ottawa, was taken into police custody after his shouting and screaming in the arrivals area had led airport staff to try to subdue him. There was no apparent reason for the shouting and screaming.

When police handcuffed him, he suddenly went into "medical distress." Paramedics tried several times to revive him before he was taken to the Ottawa Hospital's Civic campus, where he was pronounced dead.

The province's Special Investigations Unit has assigned five investigators and two forensic identification technicians to investigate what happened, particularly in regard to police involvement in the death.

The call for assistance came in through the airport's Emergency Operations Centre as a "non life-threatening" situation. Paramedics with the nearest emergency unit responded, arriving within the 20- minute window allotted for such calls. But, as they tried to care for the man, he suddenly appeared to die. Repeated attempts to revive him were unsuccessful even after he was rushed to hospital.
Special Investigations spokeswoman Kaia Werbus said investigators hope the autopsy results will "give us some answers."
She refused to say where Mr. Michaud was from.

Besides the SIU investigation, all Emergency Medical Services data is being sent to the Ministry of Health, which has been called on to do an independent review of the paramedics' actions, a standard procedure when a patient in their care dies. EMS will also review its own actions, another standard procedure, said J.P. Trottier, a spokesman for the paramedics.
Mr. Michaud was a passenger on board an Air Canada flight that left Halifax at 7:20 a.m. and arrived at the Ottawa International Airport at 8:05 a.m.
Meanwhile, the SIU is seeking witnesses who were in the area of Gate 21 at the airport Sunday after 9 a.m. Anyone with information can call the SIU at 416-622-1898 or 1-800-787-8529.
